la:noun:tellus.html:
tellūs (-ŭs short, ), ūris, f.
perh. root tollo, to bear
,
the earth, opp. to the other planets or to the sea, the globe (a word belonging almost entirely to poetry).
Lit.
In gen.: ea, quae est media et nona, tellus, neque movetur et infima, (for which: terra in medio mundo sita,; ; v. terra): animae vis aut extrinsecus aut ipsā tellure coörta, Lucr 6, 579: telluris operta subire,. —
In partic., earth, land, ground (cf. solum): quāque fuit tellus, illic et pontus et aër; Sic erat instabilis tellus, innabilis unda,; cf.: jamque mare et tellus nullum discrimen habebant; Omnia pontus erant,: nec ullis Saucia vomeribus per se dabat omnia tellus,: exercetque frequens tellurem atque imperat arvis,: reddit ubi Cererem tellus inarata,: non presso tellus exsurgit aratro,: sterilis sine arbore tellus,: fundit humo facilem victum justissima tellus,.—
Personified, Tellus, Earth, as a productive, nourishing divinity: unam eandemque terram habere geminam vim, et masculinam, quod semina producat et femininam, quod recipiat atque enutriat. Inde a vi femininā dictam esse Tellurem, a masculinā Tellumonem, Varr. ap. , 7, 23 fin.; cf.: primum (invocabo), qui omnes fructus agriculturae caelo et terrā continent, Jovem et Tellurem: itaque quod ii parentes magni dicuntur, Juppiter pater appellatur, Tellus, terra mater,; and; si est Ceres a gerendo, terra ipsa dea est: quae enim est alia Tellus?: Tellurem porco, Silvanum lacte piabant,: aedis Telluris,: in Telluris (sc. aede),: Tellus mater,.—
Transf., a land, country, district, region, territory (poet.; syn.: regio, terra): Tuscula,: tellus barbara Scythiae,; so, barbara,: Delphica,: Aegyptia,: Gnosia,: nova,: Jubae,: Assaraci, et saep.

senses: An ancient goddess of the Earth

la:noun:telum.gloss: a spear (whether used for throwing or thrusting)
senses: a spear (whether used for throwing or thrusting)
a missile or projectile weapon: an arrow, javelin, dart etc.
a stinger, prickle etc. (of natural weapons of animals and plants)
la:noun:telum.html:
tēlum, i, n.
for texlum; root τεκ-, of τίκτω, to beget; τυκ-, τυχ-, of τυγχάνω, to hit, chance upon; v. texo; cf. τόξον, a bow
,
a weapon used for fighting at a distance; a missile weapon, missile, as a dart, spear, javelin, etc. (while arma signifies arms for defence or close fight; v. arma; cf.: jaculum, tormentum).
Lit.: tela proprie dici videntur ea, quae missilia sunt: ex Graeco videlicet translato eorum nomine, quoniam illi τηλόθεν missa dicunt, quae nos eminus; sicut arma ea, quae ab umeris dependentia retinentur manibus, Müll.; cf. ; and ; : telum vulgo quidem id appellatur, quod ab arcu mittitur, sed nunc omne significatur, quod mittitur manu. Itaque sequitur, ut et lapis et lignum et ferrum hoc nomine contineatur, dictum ab eo, quod in longinquum mittitur, Graecā voce figuratum ἀπὸ τοῦ τηλοῦ, : arma rigent, horrescunt tela, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 177 Vahl.); so, opp. arma,; ; ; : tela manu jacere, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 438 Vahl.); cf.: si quis jaciat volatile telum,: tela depellere...telum jacere,: conicere,; ; ; 2, 27; ; cf.: nubes levium telorum conjecta obruit aciem Gallorum,; and with this cf.: it toto turbida caelo Tempestas telorum ac ferreus ingruit imber,: telum ex loco superiore mittere,: Romani omni genere missilium telorum ac saxis maxime vulnerabantur,; cf. Sisenn. ap. : priusquam ad conjectum teli veniretur,: tela vitare,: telis repulsi,; : non primus Teucer tela Cydonio Direxit arcu,: in medios telum torsisti primus Achivos,: tela spargere,; : aërias telum contendit in auras,: telum volatile sensit,: volucre,: hic confixum ferrea texit Telorum seges,: nubes telorum,: nimbus,. —
Transf.
In gen., an offensive weapon of any kind, as a sword, dagger, poniard, axe, etc. (class.): Ajax gladio incubuit; Ulixes intervenit ... e corpore cruentum telum educit,: ex quibus (telis) ille maximum sicarum numerum et gladiorum extulit,: elatam securim in caput dejecit: relictoque in vulnere telo ambo se foras eiciunt,: non tuba terruerit, non strictis agmina telis,: tela aliis hastae, aliis secures erant,: clavae tela erant,: stare in comitio cum telo,; so esp. freq.: esse cum telo,to be armed,; ; ; ; cf.: esse cum telo hominis occidendi causā (lex) vetat,: qui caedem telo quocumque commiserint,: ut pereat positum rubigine telum,my sheathed sword, et saep.: pars caret altera telo Frontis,i. e. a horn,; so of the caestus,; .—
Poet., like the Gr. βέλος (v. Lidd. and Scott, sub voce),
A sunbeam: non radii solis neque lucida tela diei,; ; ; 6, 40.—
Lightning: arbitrium est in sua tela Jovi,: excutere irato tela trisulca Jovi,.—
A stitch in the side, ; cf. .—
= membrum virile, ; ; . —
Trop., a weapon, shaft, dart (class.), : usque quāque sapere oportet: id erit telum acerrimum, Poët. ap. ; cf.: nec mediocre telum ad res gerendas existimare oportet benevolen, tiam civium, : nec gelidis torpet telis perfixa pavoris,: Veneris telis accipere ictus,: necessitas, quae ultimum ac maximum telum est,; : quā lege tribunitiis rogationibus telum acerrimum datum est,: de corpore rei publicae tuorum scelerum tela revellere,: tela fortunae,: lucubrationis telum,: vis tribunicia, telum a majoribus libertati paratum,; : sentire et linguae tela subire tuae,.

senses: warp (threads that run lengthwise in a loom)
la:noun:tela.html:
tēla, ae, f.
prob. contr. from texia, from texo; cf. ala, from axilla; mala, from maxilla,
,
a web.
Lit.: texentem telam studiose ipsam offendimus,: Penelope telam retexens,: tenui telas discreverat auro,; : vetus in telā deducitur argumentum,: commenta retexere tela,; ; : lanā et telā victum quaeritans,; cf.: assiduis exercet bracchia telis,: antiquas exercet telas,: plena domus telarum,.—Of a spider's web: deiciamque eorum (araneorum) omnis telas,; ; ; .—
Transf.
The threads that run lengthwise in the loom, the warp (syn.: stamen, trama),: licia telae Addere, ; ; ; sq.—
A weaver's beam, yarn-beam; also, a loom, ; ; ; . —
Trop., a web, i. e. a plan, design: exorsa haec tela non male omnino mihi est,: ad detexundam telam,: quamquam ea tela texitur et ea incitatur in civitate ratio vivendi, ut, etc.,.

la:noun:telis.html:
tēlis, is, f., = τῆλις,
the herb fenugreek Trigonella foenum Graecum, Linn.: foenum Graecum quod telin vocant,.

la:other:Telmessus.gloss: A prosperous city of Lycia situated on a bay
senses: A prosperous city of Lycia situated on a bay
la:other:Telmessus.html:
Telmessus, Telmissus, or Tel-mēsus, i, f., = Τελμησσος or Τελμισσός,
a town in Lycia, near to Caria, at the head of the Glaucus Sinus, now Makri; it was famed for the skill of its inhabitants in divination, ; ; ; .—Hence,
Telmessĭcus (Telmissĭcus, -mē-sicus), a, um, adj., of or belonging to Telmessus, Telmessian: Telmissicus sinus, Telmessicum vinum, .—
Telmissĭus, a, um, adj., of Telmissus, Telmissian. Ptolemaeus, .—As subst.Telmissĭi, ōrum, m., the innabitants of Telmissus, the Telmissians: Castra Telmissium, Drak. N. cr. (s. l. v.).—
Telmesses (-me-ses), ĭum, m., ; or Tel-messenses, ĭum, m., the inhabitants of Telmessus, the Telmessians, . —
Telmessis, ĭdis, adj. f., Telmessian: sinus,.
